title: Header Organization Constraint vs Monolithic Implementation
description: Fact 1 constrains against creating new header files and mandates using existing structure, while Fact 2 describes a monolithic 5830-line types.h file containing ALL type definitions. This massive single-file approach violates good header file structure principles that Fact 1 aims to preserve. A well-established header structure would typically distribute definitions across multiple focused headers rather than concentrating everything in one enormous file, making these facts incompatible in practice.
fact_1_statement: DO NOT create new header files, use existing well-established header file structure
fact_2_statement: types.h contains 5830 lines with ALL struct and type definitions

title: Custom Memory Management Constraint vs Direct stdlib Usage
description: Fact 1 establishes a constraint that raw malloc/free should never be used in favor of a custom memory management system. However, Fact 2 describes SET_STRING macro as 'freeing old and allocating new', which implies it uses the forbidden raw free/malloc functions rather than the required custom memory management system. This creates a direct conflict between the stated constraint and the implementation.
fact_1_statement: The MUD uses a custom memory management system - never use raw malloc/free
fact_2_statement: SET_STRING(pointer, value) macro performs safe string assignment by freeing old and allocating new

evidence.detail: Fact 1 establishes a constraint that raw malloc/free should never be used in favor of a custom memory management system. This creates a direct conflict between the stated constraint and the implementation.

title: Docker-First Constraint vs Localhost Configuration
description: Fact 1 specifies localhost:5432 for database access, which typically indicates local development setup. This conflicts with Fact 2's Docker Compose multi-service architecture, where services should communicate via container names/service names rather than localhost. In a proper Docker Compose setup, the database would be accessed via its service name (e.g., 'postgres:5432') not 'localhost:5432', unless port mapping is being used inconsistently across the architecture.
